title: What Does Electoral Victory Look Like? Visualizing Mayor Pete Buttigieg's Win
period: 2015 municipal primary (Democratic mayoral primary; city clerk race)
method: Descriptive precinct- and district-level comparison of vote margins using public City of South Bend and county results; no statistical modeling.
finding_summary: Buttigieg won 80 of 85 precincts and all six council districts in a 78-22 win over Henry Davis Jr.; Davis won four precincts in District 2 and one in District 6. The strongest precinct (Sunnymede, near IUSB) gave Buttigieg about 96 percent. The author interprets the result as broad support across neighborhoods with different socioeconomic profiles.
limits: One primary election; no demographic or income data linked to precincts; the interpretation is the author's, not a tested finding.

title: Election data suggest shifting political landscape in Indiana
geography: All 92 Indiana counties, including St. Joseph
period: 2024 presidential and governor general elections (some comparison with 2016)
method: County-by-county review of presidential and governor results, presented in tables; official data source not named.
finding_summary: St. Joseph was one of four counties (with Marion, Monroe and Lake) that Donald Trump did not carry in 2024: Harris 50.0 percent, Trump 48.5 percent. In the governor race, Jennifer McCormick took 49.8 percent in St. Joseph and Mike Braun 47.2 percent.
limits: Statewide coverage; the St. Joseph portion is a results table, not an analysis of why areas voted differently; no demographic comparison.
